children: By Sherry Qin and Amanda Lee
Taiwan's central bank kept interest rates unchanged for a tenth consecutive quarter.
The decision was expected to be a close call, with economists polled by The Wall Street Journal nearly evenly split on whether policymakers would raise rates or hold the line.

The latter camp got it right, as the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) opted to maintain the benchmark discount rate at 2.000%. Secured and unsecured lending rates were left at 2.375% and 4.250%, respectively.

Consumer inflation has printed above the central bank's 2% warning level for four months, but strong economic growth fueled by AI provides space to hold off on the rate hikes that many other central banks have already resorted to since the Iran war broke out.
